questions.q: According to the summary, what should you do after helping a superior solve a problem?
a: Give the credit away so you gain responsibility in return
Claim the credit so your skills are finally noticed
Share it equally in front of the rest of the team
Downplay the problem so nobody thinks less of her
questions.why: Lesson 1 says superiors must not look powerless; credit given away comes back as responsibility.

questions.q: Why did Nicolas Fouquet end up in prison?
a: The king accused him of stealing, since no subject could be that wealthy
He refused to finance the king's next war
He named his discoveries after a rival noble
He lost the king's money in a failed venture
questions.why: Lesson 1: Fouquet's lavish party made the king feel powerless, so he was accused of theft.

questions.q: How did Galileo secure years of funding for his research?
a: He named Jupiter's moons after his patron and his brothers
He dedicated his telescope to the French king
He let the Grand Duke claim the discovery
He taught the Duke's sons mathematics for free
questions.why: Lesson 1: Cosimo II rewarded Galileo with a court post after the moons were named for his family.

questions.q: According to the summary, why does unpredictable behavior help against competitors?
a: It disrupts their analysis while you prepare your next move
It makes your skills appear greater than they are
It pushes rivals to copy your established pattern
It signals that you have nothing left to lose
questions.why: Lesson 2: deliberate errors throw rivals off their analysis, like a bluff at a poker table.

questions.q: What does the story of Chuko Liang and King Menghuo illustrate?
a: Generosity and repeated release can win voluntary surrender
Overwhelming force is the fastest route to loyalty
Hostages should be held until a treaty is signed
Public humiliation makes rivals abandon a campaign
questions.why: Lesson 3: Liang fed and freed Menghuo seven times until he yielded on his own.
